correctness.rationale: The effective hash difference has a two-level collision atom (2m−1)/m² and uniform remaining masses. Conditional leaf-sign orthogonality decomposes the centered squared norm into factor-only and rectangle terms. Their variances are exactly 2qa, 2qb and 2Uab, including the even-width double-solution count gcd(2,m); no independence of all tensor-coordinate signs is incorrectly assumed. Fourth-power convexity gives the unique constant-magnitude maximizers. An actual independently implemented three-layer program passed 395 exact modular checks, 3190 finite extremal comparisons and 8 seeded direct simulations. This establishes the stated finite and asymptotic claims under the explicit 4-wise sign and independent-layer assumptions; experiments supplement the proof.

value.rationale: The newly proposed 2026 estimator has a generic degree-dependent variance estimate, while this exact, sharp model quantifies sketch-width requirements for the first nontrivial recursive tree. The two-level collision atom and parity-sensitive modular intersection expose which effects depend on the architecture rather than on tensor-factor fourth moments. The full all-d,m extremizer classification for separable rank-one PSD inputs is a natural benchmark for trace estimation and separates a sharp leading coefficient of 10 from the motivating general bound without claiming an improved guarantee for arbitrary PSD inputs.
